chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the falcon and the hawk among the birds of prey, are they [permissible]? He said, 'Yes, in the status of dogs.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: In the status of / equivalent to

ai.seo_question: Are falcons and hawks halal or haram to eat according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) classifies falcons and hawks as having the same status as dogs regarding ritual impurity (*najāsah*) and consumption. This ruling extends the general principle of canine impurity to birds of prey, establishing a clear jurisprudential precedent for their exclusion from permissible food (*halal*) in Shia fiqh. The comparison highlights the continuity of prophetic tradition in distinguishing between domesticated animals and wild predators based on their nature and utility.
